ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and franchisors against the consolidated Swiss SECO sanctions list, the UN Security Council sanctions measures as implemented by Swiss law, the EU restrictive measures adopted by Switzerland, and available PEP databases, with refresh upon any change of UBO or board composition, in accordance with AMLA and FINMA Circular 2023/1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX (Zentraler Firmenindex / Indice centrale des raisons de commerce) operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be in Latin script; names in German, French or Italian are privileged but genuine Latin-script transliterations of non-Latin trade names are permissible. The corporate name of an AG must include the statutory suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', 'Société anonyme', 'SA', or 'Società anonima', and the name must not be misleading or infringe third-party trademark rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Confederation / Schweiz / Helvetia / Suisse / Svizzera (unless Swissness criteria met)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal from the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant may file a written appeal with that office within 30 days from notification. If the refusal is sustained, the applicant may petition the Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) under applicable cantonal within 10 days. The applicant may simultaneously submit a modified name proposal without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual mailbox without a physical office and responsible local representative does not satisfy Swiss commercial register practice. For a franchise licensing and syrups supply chain entity, a registered office provided by a licensed corporate services fiduciary is accepted if Swiss books, minutes and official correspondence are physically retrievable at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; approximately 5% annual probability in the absence of tax or permit irregularities, rising to 20-30% if the entity applies for VAT refunds or enters significant intra-group cross-border royalty flows, as Cantonal Tax Administrations and the Commercial Register Office retain risk-based unannounced inspection powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft/AG); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Arts. 64-73; OR Art. 626 (mandatory content of Articles of Association); OR Art. 652g (blocked bank confirmation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug), Grafenau 2, 6301 Zug; federal transparency via the central name index Zefix.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister (Application for entry into the Commercial Register), filed electronically via a ZertES certified signature or through the notary's channel, attaching the notarized foundation deed and bank confirmation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000 (OR Art. 621); at least 20% of the nominal value, and in no case less than CHF 20,000, must be paid up before registration; the paid-in funds must be deposited in a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) of a licensed Swiss bank and confirmed by an irrevocable bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) issued under OR Art. 652g; the funds remain blocked until the Commercial Register entry is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CH_AG: RESOLVED that (1) the directors accept the founding shareholders' subscriptions and confirm the paid-up share capital; (2) the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Association within the Canton of Zug; (3) the Chairman of the Board, Delegate of the Board, Managing Director, and Assistant Manager are appointed with the signatory powers defined in the organization regulations; (4) the Chairman is authorized to file the Commercial Register application, to publish the entry in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, and to complete Federal Tax Administration registration. The directors certify that the blocked capital remains unencumbered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Name Pre-Clearance of the Articles of Association (Statuten)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of the Canton of Zug and the Commercial Register pre-consultation via Zefix
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss civil law notary to draft the Articles of Association satisfying OR Art. 626 (corporate name, registered office, purpose, share capital, share types, organization). Verify name availability and obtain pre-clearance from the Commercial Register Office through the Zefix portal. Prepare the notarial deed (öffentliche Beurkundung) and the foundation report (Gründungsbericht) including any contribution in kind statement.
required_dossiers: Valid passport of each founder and director
Proof of residential or corporate address of each founder
Draft Articles of Association (OR Art. 626 content)
Zefix name availability search result
International sanctions and politically exposed person declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to conflict with a prior right, select an alternative corporate name and re-submit the pre-clearance; any defective statutory clause is amended by a notarial supplementary deed within the objection window set by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account (Sperrkonto) and Obtaining Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., UBS Switzerland AG or Zürcher Kantonalbank) with a branch in the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked bank account in the name of the company in formation; transfer at least CHF 20,000 (20% of the CHF 100,000 minimum nominal capital) from each subscriber; obtain an irrevocable blocked-account confirmation (Bankbestätigung) under OR Art. 652g stating that the paid-up capital is freely disposable by the board upon registration; the account must remain blocked until the Commercial Register entry is effected.
required_dossiers: Sperrkonto account opening form
Bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung)
Founding shareholders' payment orders (SWIFT/IBAN references)
Anti-money laundering onboarding package (KYC forms under the GwG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the origin of funds under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, supply notarized evidence of lawful source; if the query persists, substitute a second licensed Swiss bank and reissue the blocked-account confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Foundation Deed and Execution of the Constituent Assembly (Gründungsversammlung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary of the Canton of Zug and the founding shareholders' meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and hold the constituent assembly before the notary; adopt the Articles of Association; elect the board of directors; decide on audit exemption (Verzicht auf die eingeschränkte Revision) where permitted under OR Art. 727a; certify the paid-in capital confirmation; sign the foundation minutes (Gründungsprotokoll) and the registration declaration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung).
required_dossiers: Notarized foundation deed (Errichtungsakt)
Foundation minutes with the adopted agenda
List of subscribed shares and founders' subscription declarations
Bank confirmation from Step 2
Articles of Association signed by all founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any founding defect such as a missing signature or an incomplete board election is cured by an additional notarial corrective deed (Nachtrag) before submission; the cure is documented and re-delivered to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Commercial Register Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug via the Swiss Federal electronic register channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Anmeldung zur Eintragung through a ZertES certified electronic signature or through the notary's account; attach the notarized foundation deed, foundation minutes, bank confirmation, board members' authenticated signatures, and declarations of no bankruptcy proceedings; pay the registration fee (approx. CHF 600) and publication fee (approx. CHF 300) upon invoicing.
required_dossiers: Completed Anmeldung zur Eintragung form
Notarized foundation deed and foundation minutes
Bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung)
List of directors with authenticated signatures
Declaration of no pending bankruptcy or enforcement proceedings against the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (Zwischenverfügung), respond in writing to the Handelsregisteramt within the granted term, typically 30 days; supply missing exhibits or amend the Articles of Association by notarial ancillary deed; the registry resumes processing upon cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schweizerisches Handelsblatt (SHAB), Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Commercial Register entry is made, the register transmits the company data to SHAB for official publication; the published entry includes corporate name, seat, purpose, share capital, board composition, and signatory powers; third parties may rely on the published facts after the publication date.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract evidencing the completed entry
SHAB publication order reference (EAN/BAR identifier) assigned by the register file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains a material error, request a rectification from the registrar so an official correction is published; verify the notice immediately because third parties may rely on the erroneous text until correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Cantonal Tax and VAT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV) and Kantonales Steueramt Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the company's UID business identification number through the EHRA identity service; register for corporate income tax, capital tax, and value added tax (Mehrwertsteuer) with ESTV when taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 annually; submit Form 0170 for VAT registration; the UID is used in all tax correspondence and invoicing.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Zefix)
Articles of Association and UID statement
Estimated turnover declaration for VAT purposes
Board resolution appointing tax representatives in Switzerland, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If UID or VAT issuance is delayed or queried, contact the EHRA Identity Service for direct UID allocation; if ESTV requests missing data, provide projected turnover and the registered purpose statement within the 15-day statutory response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security, Accident Insurance, and Occupational Health Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ausgleichskasse Zug (SWICA Compensation Office) and Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the AG with the cantonal compensation office for old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV); receive the social insurance number; register with SUVA under the food and beverage trade tariff for mandatory occupational accident insurance (UVG); arrange HACCP-based staff training and kitchen hygiene checks where the franchise support kitchens are operational.
required_dossiers: Company UID and Commercial Register extract
AHV registration form and specimen employment contracts
SUVA UVG insurance declaration for employees of the AG
Premises description including franchise support kitchen and syrup warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SUVA assigns a higher industry risk tariff, contest the rating with factual ISIC-5610 scope data and request a tariff revision; any outstanding payroll data submission is cured prospectively with the compensation office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Kantonales Amt für Lebensmittelsicherheit und Tiergesundheit Zug (Cantonal Food Safety and Veterinary Office of Zug) in cooperation with the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV/OSAV) for cross-border import of syrups and flavor concentrates.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Betriebsbewilligung für Lebensmittelbetrieb (Operating License for a Food Business) under Art. 8 of the Swiss Food and Commodities Act (LMG) and the HACCP-based Food Hygiene Ordinance (LHV); supplementary approval for the syrup packaging and boba cold-chain warehouse under cantonal food control regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Bundesamt für Umwelt (BAFU / Federal Office for the Environment) with cantonal enforcement by Amt für Umweltschutz Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not subject to a formal EIA: no Annex 1 USG capacity thresholds are reached by a beverage-preparation and syrup-packaging back-office operation; an environmental registration (Art. 10c USG) is required with the cantonal office for the building usage and wastewater connection permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to the public sewer per local connection permit with COD levels not exceeding 250 mg/l under the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV); VOC exhaust air from syrup filling must comply with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV) limit of 150 mg C/m3; waste streams segregated and disposed under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA); refrigerants in boba cold-chain equipment must be ODP-free per the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ORRChem).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety authorization (Feuerpolizeiliche Bewilligung) from the Zug Feuerpolizei validating escape routes, fire doors, and extinguishing systems for the office and syrup warehouse; structural loading certificate from the municipal building control confirming floor load capacity for syrup storage racks; occupational safety clearance from SUVA covering workplace inspection and accident prevention measures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV; Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC), Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; e-filing and registration through easygov.swiss and the TIA (VAT Identification Application).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarize the articles of incorporation and register the AG in the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister/Registre du commerce); the Commercial Register automatically allocates the federal business identifier UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and enters the company into the Zefix database. Step 2: Apply for VAT registration with the ESTV, which converts the UID into the final VAT number (MWST-Nr/TVA-Nr) using the UID edge code MWST; non-resident shareholders need no local fiscal agent, but a Swiss domicile address is required for the registered office. Step 3: For a corporate franchise/licensing AG, confirm profit-tax jurisdiction with the cantonal tax administration after incorporation; the canton issues the visible tax booklet and assessment notice. Step 4: A foreign parent licensing IP into Switzerland must obtain its own Swiss UID and VAT registration if it makes taxable supplies in Switzerland with no reverse-charge exemption; foreign entities may alternatively rely on the domestic franchisee's reverse-charge mechanism only for service supplies, not for goods.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Swiss-resident Aktiengesellschaft is fully opaque and subject to federal corporate income tax at an effective rate of approximately 7.83%, plus cantonal and communal profit taxes at a combined typical burden of 11.9% to 21.0% depending on the canton; the AG is also liable for cantonal capital tax; no pass-through to shareholders). Territorial_Scope: Swiss-resident companies are subject to worldwide taxation, but profits from foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate are exempt under applicable double-taxation treaties with full exemption method; a Swiss participation exemption (95% of qualifying dividends and capital gains) reduces the effective burden on foreign franchise subsidiaries and royalty-holding structures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election is available; an AG is mandatorily an entity-level taxpayer. However, the following statutory elections are available: (i) VAT group election under Art. 21 of the Swiss VAT Act, allowing the Swiss franchise holding company and its domestic subsidiaries to be treated as a single taxable person; (ii) participation exemption election for 95% of dividend income and capital gains from qualifying foreign and Swiss subsidiaries; (iii) deemed interest/notional-interest deduction on surplus equity under the 2019 Swiss tax reform; (iv) partial direct federal tax election for liquidation proceeds; (v) hybrid mismatch rules (implemented per OECD BEPS Action 2) are mandatory and deny deductions for payments that are deductible in Switzerland but not taxed in the recipient state, with no elective opt-out; (vi) both foreign and domestic entities may elect the small-business VAT procedure under CHF 100,000 turnover, limited to Swiss-resident suppliers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover for Swiss-resident enterprises (Art. 10 VAT Act); non-resident suppliers with taxable supplies in Switzerland are liable from the first franc unless the recipient is liable and the reverse-charge mechanism applies; a CHF 150,000 threshold applies only to non-profit and charitable associations; voluntary registration is permitted above the threshold only for legitimate business purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous-transaction-control (CTC) system, or government digital stamping mandate. Since 2020, the QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is mandatory for all invoice payments using Swiss reference numbers (ISR) and is the de facto standard for B2B franchise supply chains; the format must embed the creditor UID/VAT number and QR-IBAN. XML-based electronic invoices (FacturX, Swiss eBill) are accepted for audit purposes, but there is no central tax authority API clearance database or automatic e-invoicing validation before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods to destinations outside Switzerland is zero-rated under Art. 23(1) of the Swiss VAT Act provided the goods physically leave Swiss customs territory; services directly connected with exported goods (logistics, processing of bubble-tea syrups and packaging for foreign franchisees), transport services, and services of intermediaries acting in the name of the customer may be zero-rated. Franchise royalty and licensing services supplied to foreign franchisees are zero-rated if the service is deemed provided abroad (Art. 18(2) B2B territoriality rule) and the foreign franchisee is the taxable person receiving the benefit; intra-group service charges to a Swiss-registered central supply hub remain standard-rated at 8.1%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss e-dec/NCTS declaration) with the customs exit confirmation stamp or electronic proof of release into exportation
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, CIM/smgs, or Air Waybill evidencing physical transport of the goods out of Swiss territory
Commercial invoice with the exporter's UID/VAT number, the zero-rating reference, and a clear description of the exported goods
Franchise agreement, purchase order, delivery note, and inventory records linking the exported syrup batch to the overseas franchisee
Bank inward remittance certificate / SWIFT MT103 confirmation demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds in a Swiss bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV conducts standard documentary audits of export zero-rating claims; if the exporter cannot substantiate physical export within the audit files, the VAT is reassessed at 8.1% standard rate plus interest from the supply date. Deliberate misdeclaration to obtain an unjustified VAT benefit constitutes tax evasion under Art. 96 of the VAT Act, punishable by a fine of up to four times the evaded tax, seizure of the clawback, and publication of the decision; grossly negligent errors trigger a fine of up to one-quarter of the evaded tax. Repeated violations place the taxpayer in the ESTV KONTEST high-risk database, suspending VAT refund privileges and triggering mandatory banking disclosures to the Federal Tax Administration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht FINMA
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland has no general exchange-control regime. The Swiss franc is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and royalty payments to non-residents are unrestricted, subject only to corporate law solvency requirements, treaty anti-abuse provisions, and Swiss withholding tax at 35% (recoverable or reduced under tax treaties). No authorization from the SNB is required for foreign direct investment, inbound equity injections, or outbound settlement. Capital flows are only subject to statistical reporting obligations under the Financial Statistics Ordinance (Finanzstatistikverordnung, FStatV) when cumulative cross-border payments reach CHF 1 million within a 30-day period, which is satisfied via the resident bank's reporting duty rather than by the corporate client.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or minimum conversion ratio requiring mandatory surrender of export proceeds in Switzerland. Exporters are free to hold export receipts in foreign currency or convert them through any licensed bank. The only mandatory obligation is statistical in nature: movements exceeding CHF 1 million per counterparty per month must be reported to the SNB via the clearing bank using prescribed balance-of-payments codes. For the bubble tea franchise model, franchise royalty inflows from Swiss stores are classified as service receipts (royalty/licensing income) and are not subject to any conversion or repatriation restriction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse AG (now integrated into UBS AG)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for licensed Swiss fintechs and FINMA-licensed payment institutions; Low for offshore digital EMI operators that lack a FINMA licence or Swiss banking foothold. Swiss corporate treasury policy for a CH_AG franchise royalty and syrup supply business should prefer FINMA-supervised entities (e.g., licensed fintech banks under Banking Act Art. 1b) for cross-border collections and disbursements. Offshore EMIs (e.g., non-EU/EEA digital wallets, unlicensed payment aggregators) can legally be used as collection overlay in limited amounts, but they create AML concentration risk, may be viewed unfavourably by Swiss bankers, and cannot provide Swiss IBAN-based clearing for domestic store credit-card POS settlement without a banking licence or partnership with a licensed Swiss bank. For franchise royalty collection from global franchisees, SWIFT-based commercial bank rails remain the primary compliant option; EMIs are viable only as supplementary collection vehicles for low-value payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not always mandatory, but Swiss banks generally require a personal identity verification for at least one signatory director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO). Many major Swiss banks offer remote video-identification (video-ident) for natural persons, but for a corporate AG with non-resident shareholders and directors, the accepted lower-risk route is a physical meeting at the bank counter or a verified remote interview with simultaneous authentication of the passport and residence permit, augmented by apostilled corporate documents. In practice, for expiry of account opening and to combat de-risking, at least one executive director and the UBO should appear in person at a Swiss bank branch. If no director can travel, banks usually require an external KYC interview conducted by a Swiss notary, registered agent, or a correspondent bank in the director's jurisdiction; the interview must be minuted and authenticated. For UBS and PostFinance, remote opening for a limited company is possible only if the company is already established, the UBO identity is verifiable against high-integrity identity sources, and the bank's compliance officer approves the digital dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO structure involving non-resident shareholders domiciled in a high-risk or unclear-source-wealth jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract (Handelsregisterauszug), apostilled articles of association, group structure chart, UBO declaration form, executed shareholder register, audited financial statements or proof of capital (opening balance sheet), notarized source-of-wealth statements, bank references from the shareholder's home-country regulated bank, and clean public-record screening reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction profile involving global franchise royalty receipts and syrup trade settlements with multiple counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, franchise agreement template, royalty calculation model, sample supply-chain invoices, list of licensed stores with jurisdictions, bill-of-lading and sales contract evidence for syrup exports, and an annual projected cash-flow statement classified by counterparty jurisdiction to demonstrate a rational, low-risk trade and licensing pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency low-ticket payments from franchise stores via local POS or card acquirers creating fragmented transaction velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Acquirer contract, settlement reports from card processors, daily store sales rollups, registered trademark licensing documentation, royalty allocation schedule, and internal controls ensuring all receipts correspond to auditable royalty agreements rather than indirect third-party collections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from the sole shareholder or related party resembling a loan-for-equity or unsecured shareholder advance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholder contribution agreement, board minutes authorising the capital increase, proof of source of funds (bank statements from the contributor), Swiss tax ruling confirming tax treatment of the contribution, and capital adequacy calculation meeting the CHF 100,000 minimum capital requirement for an AG.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment routing via offshore EMI or high-risk clearing corridor for syrup imports and franchise royalty outflows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion on the payment intermediary's licence, chain-of-custody KYC from the EMI, SWIFT MT103 records with proper purpose codes, correspondence from the Swiss bank confirming no prohibited CFT flags, and documented controls that no sanctioned jurisdictions are touched anywhere along the chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection into the CH_AG is executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the Swiss bank from the shareholder's regulated bank, using purpose code 'INVEST' or 'S3001' as accepted by the Swiss bank for equity capital contributions. The credit must be booked against the capital contribution account / capital reserve and followed by corporate-law deposit verification and notarisation for registration in the Handelsregister. For franchise-related inflows, the remittance tip should use SPFS? no, use SWIFT codes: purpose code 'ROYL' for royalty/license income and 'GDSV' for goods and services. Verification includes the bank's compliance screening of the remitter, passport of the shareholder, evidence of no tax anti-money-laundering concerns, and preservation of the SWIFT record for the statutory ten-year business-record retention period.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for syrup supplies and equipment to franchisees are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments and SWIFT MT700/MT707 for documentary collections and commercial letters of credit (LC). Payment instructions must include accurate purpose codes under the Swiss National Bank statistical classification matrix (e.g., 'S2050' for trade payments, 'S2200' for services). Trade settlement can also be executed through bank payment obligations (BPO) and standard supplier invoices with matched POB/EXW transport documents. For franchise royalty payments received from stores using local POS acquirers, the clearing rail should aggregate daily card receipts into a settlement account via Six Payment Services AG (Swiss local card clearing), then sweep via SEPA or domestic clearing into the operative SBIBAN account. International disbursement batches above CHF 1 million must be flagged under the FStatV statistical reporting requirement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Swiss-franc/currency spot contracts and plain vanilla forward contracts (up to 12 months, subject to the bank's master trading agreement) for CNY, USD, EUR and CHF exposures arising from franchise royalty receipts and syrup import payments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against restricted/emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY offshore, IDR, MYR) offered by Swiss banks with a FINMA-licensed booking entity, used only where onshore deliverability is impossible
Cross-currency swaps (mark-to-market collateralised) to match long-term syrup supply-chain contracts and foreign-currency franchise financing obligations
Currency options (call/put) purchased through regulated Swiss banks for downside protection, with no premium on prohibited speculative positions
FX swaps and swap points rolling short-term liquidity between CHF and major trade currencies, physically settled with the Swiss clearing bank, and only for hedging underlying business transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AGM annual declaration: directors' report, financial statements, profit appropriation, discharge of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public filing ordinarily; minutes kept at registered office; Commercial Register filing only for changes to directors, auditors, or capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date (Art. 699 Swiss Code of Obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene AGM triggers directors' personal liability, administrative fines, and possibly criminal liability for negligent business management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual cantonal and federal corporate income tax return with financial statements and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 180 days after fiscal year-end; extension up to 12 months possible upon approved application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest at 5% per annum, late payment interest at 3.5–5% per annum, administrative penalties up to 100% of additional tax, criminal referral for willful evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT annual reconciliation and return (or quarterly returns with annual settlement if turnover below CHF 5.5 million)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after end of reporting period; quarterly filers must submit final reconciliation by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on late VAT, penalty up to three times the tax evaded (minimum CHF 250), and administrative fine up to CHF 10,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social security (AHV/IV/EO) wage declaration and contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January of the following wage year (or as directed by the compensation office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contribution arrears interest at 5% per annum, personal employer liability, director liability for unpaid contributions, criminal sanctions for gross neglect

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner register self-certification and share register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's corporate records; made available without delay to Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) and prosecution authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual board certification by 31 December; immediate update within 10 working days of any share transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of Swiss AML Act is a criminal offense: fines up to CHF 500,000; directors individually liable for damage caused by failure to maintain accurate registers

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit required for two consecutive years if any two of three thresholds exceeded: balance sheet total > CHF 20 million; gross turnover > CHF 40 million; annual average > 250 full-time employees. Public or regulated companies always require ordinary audit. Limited audit is required for SMEs unless an opt-out is validly approved by all shareholders; opt-out available only if company does not exceed any two of: balance sheet total < CHF 3 million; turnover < CHF 6 million; < 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting principles (OR Art. 957–963), supplemented by Swiss GAAP FER for complete financial statements; IFRS permitted for listed and financial-sector entities; SME simplified presentation allowed under commercial code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not require annual public filing of beneficial owners. The company must maintain and verify the share register and UBO register annually by board resolution. Every share transfer requires board approval, a written confirmation to the transferor, and immediate update of the Aktienbuch. The updated register must be available at the registered office and to Swiss authorities within 24 hours for AML investigations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings
Articles of Association and Capital Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–3,000 per year depending on canton and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–15,000 for limited audit; USD 15,000–60,000 for ordinary audit of a mid-sized Aktiengesellschaft

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal headline rate, equal to 7.83% on a pre-tax basis; combined effective burden with cantonal and communal taxes approximately 11.6% in Zug (Canton of Zug) and 19.7% in Zurich, with a Swiss national average between 11% and 21% depending on the commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. The TRAF (Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act, effective 2020) provides a Patent Box deduction (up to 90% of qualifying IP income derived from Swiss R&D), an R&D additional deduction (up to 50% in adopting cantons), a Notional Interest Deduction (available in selected cantons including Zug, Zurich and Geneva), and Participation Relief (qualifying dividend and capital gains income from shareholdings of at least 10% or with a market value above CHF 1 million are substantially tax exempt).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss legal entities file a unified annual tax declaration ('Steuererklärung für juristische Personen') covering federal direct tax and cantonal/communal taxes. The federal filing is administered through the FTA eTax desk; cantonal e-filing portals include Zug 'Taxonline' and Zurich 'ZüriTax eFiling'. MWSV/VAT returns are lodged separately on the FTA Swiss GST portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax returns must generally be filed within 6 to 8 months after the close of the fiscal year (calendar-year taxpayers in most cantons face an initial deadline of 30 June or 30 September). Extensions are granted on reasoned request; failure to obtain an extension triggers reminder procedure and compulsory assessed taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name of the Aktiengesellschaft, UID number, seat, legal form, statutory capital and fully paid-up capital, fiscal year dates, board members and signatory powers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all non-resident shareholders, including economic beneficial owners and intermediary holding companies; for a Hong Kong or foreign UBO holding the Swiss AG, provide the full chain of ownership from the seat of the AG through each intermediate entity to the final individual to satisfy the FTA's transparency duty under Art. 46 VStG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Reconciled profit and loss (bereinigte Erfolgsrechnung)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial accounting profit with taxable net profit: franchise royalty income, syrup supply chain revenue, COGS, administration costs, non-deductible expenses (own taxes, hidden shareholder benefits, excessive depreciation), provisions and tax reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalty income from master franchisees abroad is taxable in full in Switzerland as worldwide income of the Swiss company; intercompany royalty charges payable by the Swiss AG to related foreign IP owners are deductible only if the CUP benchmark shows an arm's length rate; shareholder loans must respect the thin capitalization maximum debt-to-equity ratio of 6:1 for financing structures and 3:1 for holding structures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base after deduction of participation relief, patent box relief, notional interest deduction and loss carryforward (maximum 7 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the foreign parent intends to repatriate net profit, the Board must first declare a dividend; Board resolutions on dividends are subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax with refund/reduced-rate claims available to treaty-eligible shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable equity for cantonal/communal capital tax, calculated as paid-in share capital plus disclosed and hidden reserves and retained earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capital tax applies irrespective of foreign ownership; excess cash pools and intercompany receivables from the franchise network cannot be stripped out through artificial debt because the cantonal capital tax base recaptures direct and indirect financing loans.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual tax return: procedural fine up to CHF 10,000; reminders trigger compulsory assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) with anti-arbitrariness surcharge; late payment interest at approximately 4.5% p.a.; intentional tax evasion: fine up to 3 times the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); qualified criminal tax fraud: imprisonment up to 3 years (Art. 186 DBG).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividend distributions, payable by the Swiss paying company before distribution; a 10-day quarantine period applies to dividend coupons after which refund liability lapses (VStG Art. 13).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident corporate shareholder may reclaim part of the 35% WHT or obtain reduced taxation through the following protocol: (i) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the tax authority of the foreign state; (ii) file FTA Form 823 (refund application for foreign legal entities) within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid; (iii) alternatively obtain prior FTA approval for reduced withholding at source by submitting Form R-22 through a Swiss paying agent; (iv) satisfy the applicable DTA conditions on beneficial ownership, holding percentage and minimum holding period, generally 0% to 15% according to the relevant treaty; (v) meet the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test - treaty benefits are denied if obtaining the reduced rate was one of the principal purposes of the structure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on ordinary cross-border arm's length royalties or on ordinary debt interest payments (only interest on Swiss domestic bonds, and interbank money-market instruments, attracts the 35% ABV). The statutory rate for royalty and interest is therefore 0%; treaty rates normally lead to 0% royalty WHT and 0% to 10% interest WHT depending on the residence state. Caution: outbound franchise royalty and syrup supply-chain wire transfers are nonetheless subject to Swiss VAT - the standard 8.1% VAT rate applies to franchise or trademark license fees, while physical bubble-tea food products benefit from the reduced 2.6% VAT rate; the place-of-supply rules for intangibles normally locate the supply in the state of the recipient, triggering reverse-charge declaration in the destination state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland has no statutory Local File threshold, but FTA and cantonal practice require full transfer pricing documentation (Local File equivalent) for taxpayers with annual domestic turnover exceeding CHF 80 million or intra-group revenues exceeding CHF 20 million when raised in an audit; CbC reporting obligation applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) - preferred for franchise royalty benchmarking
Resale Price Method - for syrup and packaging distribution subsidiaries
Cost Plus Method - for bottling or preparation service entities
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) - for distribution and procurement platforms
Profit Split Method - for integral global value chains with unique intangibles
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain a Gulf-state style Economic Substance Regulation, but the OECD MLI and the TRAF anti-abuse rules impose a substantive de facto presence requirement to obtain treaty benefits, participation relief and WHT refunds. The Swiss franchise royalty company must maintain: a physical registered office with a local director, employees with actual technical and managerial skills, board meetings held in Switzerland, independent decision-taking, adequate bank accounts and a documented commercial rationale for the intellectual property development and licensing. An AG that is merely a letterbox conduit without these attributes is treated as fiscally transparent or as a sham, with all foreign passive income re-attributed to the ultimate foreign shareholders and 35% WHT clawed back together with penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional under-invoicing of franchise royalties or syrup transfer prices to shift profits to zero-tax jurisdictions of the Hong Kong parent; the creation of a shelf AG with no commercial staff; concealment of franchisee cash royalty payments; use of cryptocurrency round-tripping to channel franchise license fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 3 times the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); aggravated commercial tax fraud carries imprisonment up to 3 years (Art. 186 DBG); unpaid tax plus statutory default interest at 4.5% p.a. is assessed within a certificate of debt (Rechtsöffnung) and enforceable through cantonal debt collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable as principals or accessories; the federal tax assessment is transposed into a personal claim against the responsible director for the evaded amount; Swiss criminal conviction triggers automatic asset seizure, possible travel restriction within the Schengen visa system, extradition exposure and disqualification from board membership for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Swiss AG incorporated with nominal share capital of only CHF 100,000, no employees, no premises, board composed exclusively of professional nominees, and management physically carried out in Hong Kong; misuse of the abolished mixed-company status (end of 2019) for structure which has no genuine Swiss channel; aggressive use of a Hong Kong entity as beneficial owner to avoid reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of participation relief and of DTA treaty protection; re-qualification of accumulated profits as hidden distributions subject to 35% WHT; adjustment of taxable income by the FTA using a discretionary assessment, plus interest and penalties; forced dissolution of the company without substance is obtainable by the cantonal registration authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability to the tax administration under Art. 754 OR for unlawful reduction of assets; criminal proceedings for fiscal misrepresentation expose board members to fines and up to 3 years imprisonment; UBOs behind nominee directorships are exposed to criminal restraint orders, impoundment of Swiss real estate, and revocation of Swiss residence permits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting master-franchise fees and royalty wires without verifying beneficial ownership of bank counterparties; routing franchise payments through high-risk fintech PSPs or cryptocurrencies without KYC; structuring payments amounts below CHF 10,000 reporting thresholds; deliberately concealing the economic beneficiary of the Swiss AG behind bearer shares or nominee ownership in Hong Kong.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis StGB: imprisonment up to 3 years (5 years in aggravated cases of laundering a criminal organization's assets); corporate liability under Art. 102 StGB: fines up to CHF 5 million; administrative fines under the GwG/AMLA up to CHF 40,000 per violation; confiscation of laundered assets and proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are individually criminally accountable in their operational capacity; penalties are not insurable and are borne personally; non-resident directors face immediate arrest warrants by Swiss authorities, travel bans, international Red Notice requests, and extradition from Hong Kong or third states; civil liability under the Art. 102 StGB compliance provision pierces the corporate veil, allowing confiscation of personal bank accounts of the director held in Switzerland.
